items.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Across the street was a place called the Last Word that had a group that was lead by another tenor player named Jack McVeigh who used to work with Lionel Hampton’s band.

ctx.x: You characterize Central Avenue, or at least Los Angeles, particularly the Central Avenue scene, [as] vibrant, thriving as far as music… Can you describe the scene a little more, which clubs and which musicians you met?

Yeah, exactly. On Central Avenue, there was a club called the Downbeat. When I first went there, Howard McGee had a band there with Teddy Edwards and another tenor player named J.D. King, who used to work with Howard with Andy Kirk’s band. Across the street was a place called the Last Word that had a group that was lead by another tenor player named Jack McVeigh who used to work with Lionel Hampton’s band. On the same side of the street as the Downbeat was a place called the Club Alabam that had big bands playing…
